title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt Fits 24GB by Making the Active Path Small
excerpt: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt ships 74B total parameters with 9B active, quantized down to 2-bit, sized to fit 24GB, with Unsloth GGUFs and Ollama/LM Studio support on day one. The headline is 74B. The useful numbers are 9B active, 22GB of weights, and a 1.7GB vision projector.

title: KVARK Sparkle 1.1 Makes Refusal a UI State
excerpt: KVARK Sparkle 1.1 is a 27B document Q&A model that declines 91.5% of unanswerable questions, released under Apache 2.0.

title: Agent Memory Is a Diff Problem, Not a Graph Problem
excerpt: Rendering an agent's memory as a graph is a debugging move, and the diff view is the part that matters.

title: Split the Conversation From the Activity Stream
excerpt: The conversation stream and the activity stream are different things, and conflating them is why agent UIs feel broken.

title: CopilotKit's Vue SDK Is a Bet on the Protocol Layer
excerpt: CopilotKit now ships a native Vue SDK over AG-UI, so one agent can drive React, Vue, React Native, or Angular frontends. The bet is on the protocol layer, not the components.

title: Building a Physics Engine From First Principles at DigiPen
excerpt: I built physics-based game engines from scratch in C++ at DigiPen, and the cohort took 3 of the 4 game design awards that year. That is the fact I can verify. What I want to talk about is why building the engine first was the right call for a student program, and what I would do differently now.

title: A2UI is a trust-boundary decision, not a styling preference
excerpt: Google's A2UI is a declarative message format for agent-driven UIs, and the interesting part is not that agents can generate interfaces. It is the native-first constraint: the agent sends a blueprint of trusted components, and the client maps them to its own native widgets rather than running HTML in an iframe.

title: Heretic 2.0 makes model modification something you can test
excerpt: Heretic 2.0 replaces abliteration with Arbitrary-Rank Ablation and rebuilds model modification around a plugin pipeline you can test and repeat.

title: This Week in Agents: Export Lists and Typed Streams
excerpt: The agent news this week was mostly infrastructure hardening: regulation reached for the weights themselves, and streaming settled into typed, queued, replayable protocols.

title: The proxy is not the boundary
excerpt: An HN thread on running your own LLM proxy makes a point most agent stacks skip: the harness between you and the model is the real data boundary.

title: A thin chat frontend is a sign of maturity, not a shortcut
excerpt: TinyWebUI is a drop-in chat frontend for local models that ships as an npx command instead of a full Open WebUI stack. The interesting part is not that it exists. It is that the frontend stopped being the hard part.

title: On-Demand Agent UI Is a Sandbox Problem, Not a Rendering One
excerpt: On-demand agent UI is a sandbox problem, not a rendering one. CopilotKit's Open Intelligent UI lets an agent build charts, maps, calculators, games, and 3D scenes on demand inside your own app, streaming while it generates, with the code running in a sandboxed iframe. The generation is the easy part to demo. The boundary is the part that ships.

title: Open weights is a license question, not a size question
excerpt: Mistral Large 4 ships as open weights under a modified MIT license, with the offensive-capability variant gated behind vetting.

title: shadcn's Trace Component Treats Agent Steps as UI State
excerpt: shadcn/ui's October release adds a Trace component that renders agent steps with running, error, and pending states, plus nested lines, alongside a Code Block and AI Elements patterns. The interesting part is not the component. It is the decision to model an agent run as a tree of steps with explicit lifecycle states, in a component library that most production apps already depend on.

title: A static publishing loop: cron writes, Vite ships, Cloudflare serves
excerpt: I built a publishing loop where a cron job writes the blog and the site ships itself.

title: AG-UI lets agents drive the browser, and that is a policy problem
excerpt: AG-UI formalizes agent-to-frontend events, including tool calls that drive browser navigation. The interesting part is the trust boundary, not the protocol.

title: Chat Is a Job Transcript, Not a Conversation
excerpt: Chat breaks down once an agent starts taking real actions, and prettier components alone will not fix it.

title: This Week in Agents: From Checkpoint to Pixel
excerpt: Open weights hit every layer of the stack this week: a trillion-parameter release, the wafer-scale hardware to serve it, and a faster serialization format for agent frontends. These picks trace a path from checkpoint to browser pixel, where open models now actually get judged.

title: CPU Cache Is the Agent Isolation Boundary
excerpt: Separate microVMs exchanged secrets through processor cache when asked to find a way, which is a reminder that agent isolation is a hardware problem, not just a software one.

title: Streamed Props Are the Real Interface Contract
excerpt: Streamed props are the real interface contract between agents and UIs, not the component tree.

excerpt: Streaming is solved, composition is not: a survey of AI chat UI libraries names the real gap, and it is not token delivery.

excerpt: CopilotKit's generative UI guide splits the space into three patterns, and the split matters more than any one implementation.

excerpt: OpenAI's GPT-6 announcement leads with "intelligent UI for everyone," which is a product claim dressed up as a feature name.

excerpt: Syncfusion's A2UI maps structured model output to approved UI components instead of freeform generative UI, which is the safer trade for production agent surfaces.

title: Flint Is a Pipeline Announcement, Not a Model
excerpt: The interesting part of Flint is the pipeline that built it, not the model itself.

title: Benchmark Scores Are a Proxy, Not a Measurement

title: The Job Runner, Not the Chat Window
excerpt: Multi-step agent workflows expose the UI as the actual bottleneck: 30-second latencies, tool calls, and side effects need first-class events, not streaming text.

title: On-Device Meeting Notes: What the Privacy Constraint Forces
excerpt: The interesting part of Hobnob is not that it transcribes meetings. It is the decision to run the whole pipeline on-device, and what that decision forces you to do everywhere else.

title: Adaptive Batching for Agent UIs
excerpt: Streaming 100 tokens per second will jank your UI unless you batch adaptively with scheduler.yield().
